## Kyoto Weekend Trip Plan for Apr 10–12, 2026
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/map.svg

Balanced for 2 adults, with temples, food markets, one relaxing activity, and mostly walking + public transit. Budget target: **USD 1,200 total excluding international flights**.

## 3-Day Kyoto Itinerary with Estimated Costs
| Day | Focus | Morning | Afternoon | Evening | Est. Cost for 2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Apr 10 | Higashiyama temple walk | Kiyomizu-dera, Sannenzaka stroll | Kodai-ji, Yasaka Shrine, Gion lanes | Riverside dinner near Pontocho | USD 260–330 |
| Apr 11 | Markets + central Kyoto | Nishiki Market breakfast crawl | Nijo Castle or Kyoto Imperial Palace area | Relaxing onsen/sento or tea house time | USD 240–330 |
| Apr 12 | Arashiyama nature + temples | Bamboo Grove, Tenryu-ji | Okochi Sanso or river walk | Final meal in Kyoto Station area | USD 220–300 |

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Route
### Day 1: Higashiyama Temples and Gion
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Start early at **Kiyomizu-dera**, then walk downhill through **Sannenzaka/Ninenzaka** before crowds build.
- Afternoon: Visit **Kodai-ji** and **Yasaka Shrine**; keep the pace slow and use side streets for a scenic walk.
- Evening: Explore **Gion** and have dinner near **Pontocho** or along the Kamo River.
- Food: Matcha sweets, yuba, tofu, and a casual izakaya dinner.

### Day 2: Food Markets and a Calm Reset
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
- Morning: Do a **Nishiki Market** breakfast crawl; focus on small bites so you can sample more.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Morning: Do a **Nishiki Market** breakfast crawl; focus on small bites so you can sample more, Kyoto, Japan
- Afternoon: Choose **Nijo Castle** for history or the **Kyoto Imperial Palace** grounds for a lighter walking day.
- Evening: Add your relaxing activity: a **sento/onsen-style bath**, then a quiet tea or dessert stop.
- Food: Tamagoyaki, pickles, sesame snacks, tofu dishes, and a wagashi dessert.

### Day 3: Arashiyama and a Scenic Finish
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Go to **Arashiyama Bamboo Grove** early, then continue to **Tenryu-ji**.
- Afternoon: Walk the river area or choose **Okochi Sanso Garden** for a peaceful break with views.
- Evening: Return to central Kyoto for an easy dinner near **Kyoto Station** before departure.
- Food: Yudofu, soba, grilled skewers, or a final ramen stop.

## Rainy-Day Backup Plan
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cloud-rain.svg
- **Temple substitute:** Kyoto National Museum area or indoor temple halls with shorter outdoor transfers.
Media: Alt=Temple substitute:** Kyoto National Museum area or indoor temple halls with shorter outdoor transfers, Kyoto, Japan
- **Market substitute:** Nishiki Market stays useful in rain because much of it is covered.
- **Relaxing substitute:** Tea ceremony experience, craft shopping, or a bath-house visit.
- **Transit-friendly swap:** Use Kyoto Station, subway lines, and short taxi hops only when needed.

## Budget Fit for 2 Adults
| Category | Planned Range | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Lodging, 3 nights | USD 420–600 | Mid-range hotel or well-rated guesthouse |
| Local transit | USD 40–70 | Subway, buses, occasional taxi |
| Admissions | USD 40–90 | Temples, castle/garden entries, optional extras |
| Food | USD 260–360 | Mix of market snacks, lunch spots, and dinners |
| Relaxing activity | USD 40–90 | Sento/onsen, tea, or similar |
| Buffer | USD 120–200 | Weather, taxis, extra meals, souvenirs |
